description: An eight-step sequencer driven by a phase ramp rather than by clock pulses, so each step has its own position, length and shape within the bar, and 32 patterns are held at once.

params.text: Turns the whole pattern against the incoming phase by hand, a full cycle over its travel; it is an endless encoder, so it has no ends.
Chooses what fills the time between incoming clock pulses: lit, the tempo measured from the clock itself; unlit, the BPM knob. It comes up lit.
Sets the tempo used when no clock is being followed, 0 to 240 BPM, and the tempo the V/OCT scaling is measured up from.
Reads the phase input as an absolute position in the bar rather than as a running count, which also fixes the pattern resolution at one step per cycle and disables the jump inputs.
Disengages the transport: the phase stops advancing and the gate output falls, while everything set on the panel stays put.
Sends the phase back to the start of the pattern.
Mutes and unmutes its own step of the pattern.
Pushes every step back onto its evenly spaced position in the bar, undoing the shifts.
Rotates the whole pattern one step earlier.
Rotates the whole pattern one step later.
Sets every step back to one eighth of the bar long.
Reverses the order of the steps within the bar.
Turns every step value upside down about zero.
Inverts every step gate at once, so muted steps play and playing steps fall silent.
Slides every step earlier or later together, by up to one step length either way.
Scales every step length together, from nothing at 0 to double at 2.
Blocks the pattern-changing inputs, so a patch cannot move off the pattern being edited.
Sets how many steps of the incoming phase make one pass of the pattern, 1 to 99, and the display reads it back.
Slides the whole pattern against the bar, a full pattern either way.
Randomly nudges every step attribute a little further from what was set, by an amount that grows as the knob is turned; turning it back does not undo the change.
Sets the voltage its step sends to the V output, -2V to +2V.
Sets how long its step lasts, from nothing to a quarter of the bar.
Moves its step earlier or later within the bar, by up to one eighth either way.
Sets the level the expression output starts its step at, -1 to +1 of the ±5V output swing.
Sets the level the expression output finishes its step at, -1 to +1 of the ±5V output swing.
Chooses how the tempo input is read: V/OCT doubles the BPM knob setting per volt, V/BPS reads the voltage straight as beats per second. The word on the switch is the mode in use.

inputs.text: A clock here steps the phase forward one resolution step per pulse, and the tempo between pulses is measured from it.
A voltage here sets the tempo, scaled either as V/OCT or as V/BPS according to the switch that labels it.
A 0-10V ramp here drives the sequencer directly, in place of any internal tempo; the BPM display goes dark while it is patched.
A trigger here engages or disengages the transport.
A trigger here sends the phase back to the start of the pattern.
A trigger here jumps to the pattern named by the voltage at the pattern-select jack.
Names a pattern by voltage, a twelfth of a volt per pattern, for the GOTO trigger to jump to.
A trigger here jumps to a pattern picked at random.
A trigger here moves one place left in the pattern grid.
A trigger here moves one row down in the pattern grid.
A trigger here moves one row up in the pattern grid.
A trigger here moves one place right in the pattern grid.
A trigger here advances to the next pattern in the grid, whether or not anything has been edited into it.
A trigger here goes back to the previous pattern that has been edited away from its default.
A trigger here goes on to the next pattern that has been edited away from its default.
Above 1V here, every step gate is inverted, the same way the GATE button does it.
Slides every step earlier or later, added to the shift knob, a step length either way over ±5V.
Scales every step length, multiplying the length knob by between nothing and double over ±5V.
Bends the shape of the expression envelope for every step at once; it replaces the curve figure rather than adding to it.
Steepens or flattens the expression envelope for every step at once; it replaces the power figure rather than adding to it.
A trigger here jumps the phase straight to the start of its own step.
A trigger here jumps the phase to the start of a step picked at random from those that are not muted.
A trigger here pulls the pattern a little back toward what was set; a voltage below -1V instead clears the mutation completely.
A trigger here nudges the pattern a little further from what was set.

outputs.text: High for as long as a step is playing, with a brief drop between one step and the next while Retrigger Gate between active steps is on.
The value of the step being played, -2V to +2V.
How far the step being played has been moved from its even position, ±5V for a full step length either way.
How much longer or shorter the step being played is than one eighth of the bar, ±5V.
An envelope running across the step being played, from its start level to its end level along the curve set for it, ±5V.
The curve figure of the step being played as a steady voltage, ±5V, taken from the vertical axis of that step's expression pad.
A ramp from 0V to 10V across the step being played, restarting at every step.
A 1ms 10V trigger whenever the pattern changes.
The pattern being played, as a twelfth of a volt per pattern.
High for as long as its own step is playing.
A 1ms 10V trigger each time the phase crosses the start of the pattern running backwards.
A ramp from 0V to 10V across the whole pattern, with the manual phase offset already added.
A 1ms 10V trigger each time the phase crosses the end of the pattern running forwards.
A 1ms 10V trigger whenever the pattern wraps round, whichever direction it is running.

notes: The module runs on a phase ramp rather than on clock pulses. A ramp at the PHASE input drives it directly and overrides everything else.
With no phase ramp patched, a clock at the CLK input steps the pattern and the gaps between pulses are filled from the measured tempo; failing that a tempo voltage, failing that the knob.
The 32 patterns are laid out as four rows of eight on the small display. Clicking a cell switches to that pattern; dragging one cell onto another copies the first into the second.
The pattern grid and the large step display are each a single drawn widget, so nothing inside them can be clicked for help even though both can be edited by hand.
The square pad in each step column is one drawn widget with no clickable control behind it, so it has no help of its own.
Dragging a step's square pad sideways sets its expression power and up and down sets its curve; together they bend the shape the EXPR output takes across that step.
The large display draws the eight steps against the bar and can be edited by dragging them.
Three parameters have no widget on the panel at all: mutate, randomise and clear, left over from an earlier layout. The MUTA knob and the menu do that work now.
menu: Copy Steps To Next Pattern — writes the eight steps of this pattern over the one after it in the grid
Copy Steps To Prev Pattern — writes the eight steps of this pattern over the one before it in the grid
Copy To All Patterns — writes this pattern over all 32
Copy Reso To All Patterns — gives every pattern the resolution this one has, leaving their steps alone
Randomize All Patterns — throws new step values, lengths and shifts into all 32 patterns
Randomize All Resolutions — gives every pattern a resolution picked at random between 1 and 99
Bake Mutation — takes whatever the MUTA knob has drifted the steps to and makes it the pattern, so the mutation can be cleared without losing it
Clear Pattern — puts this pattern back to eight evenly spaced steps at 0V
Retrigger Gate between active steps — drops the gate output for a tenth of a millisecond between one step and the next, so an envelope patched to it fires again
Polyphony: Monophonic, Polyphonic 8, Muta-Unison 16 — one step at a time, or all eight on eight channels, or all eight twice on sixteen, mutated and unmutated
External CV Mode: V/OCT, V/BPS — sets how the tempo input is scaled, and moves the switch printed on the panel to match
Snap CV — rounds the tempo arrived at through the tempo input to a whole number of beats per minute
